clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes the Vice Presidential Service Badge, to be awarded in the name of the Vice President to service members assigned to duty in the Office of the Vice President for at least one year after December 19, 1974. Executive Order 13373 section 1(a)-(b) (March 10, 2005) amended it and Executive Order 14131 section 2(a) (December 20, 2024) restated it to read as the Code note prints it. No held instrument ends it, so it is operative on 2026-10-14 as amended.

clauses.reason: Section 2 says who may award the badge and on whose recommendation. Executive Order 13286 section 56 (effective March 1, 2003) replaced the Secretary of Transportation with the Secretary of Homeland Security; Executive Order 13373 section 1(c)-(d) (March 10, 2005) replaced the recommending officer and added the Secretaries of Commerce and of Health and Human Services; Executive Order 14131 section 2(b) (December 20, 2024) restated the section. These are amendments, so the clause continues as amended and is operative on 2026-10-14.

The first half of Section 7 supersedes Executive Order No. 11544 of July 8, 1970. The order contains no later effective date, so the supersession took effect when the order was signed on July 19, 1976, and the command was executed on that day. research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (41 FR 29805, July 20, 1976; jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11926.txt) is Executive Order 11926 of July 19, 1976, The Vice Presidential Service Badge, signed by the President as Commander in Chief; the order has no sunset, expiry or condition of its own. Inventory: the dossier inventory begins at Sec. 2 because the OCR renders the heading of Section 1 as 'Section  l.'; Section 1 is therefore added by inventory override, and Section 7 is split into its supersession of Executive Order 11544 (a command executed on issuance) and its proviso letting earlier badge holders keep wearing the badge (a continuing permission). Later instruments: Executive Order 13286 section 56 (effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) changed the officer named in Sec. 2; Executive Order 13373 section 1(a)-(j) (March 10, 2005) amended Secs. 1, 2, 5 and 6; Executive Order 14131 section 2(a)-(d) (December 20, 2024) restated Secs. 1, 2, 4 and 6. Each is an amendment, and under the owner's 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues as amended. The dossier's chain also lists an Executive Order 12977 entry; its quoted provision is the text of Executive Order 13286 section 56 and its source is a gap note about Executive Order 13286 section 23, so it is not a separate instrument amending this order and is not cited. Current law: the U.S. Code note named in each clause is a held CURRENT record; every instrument cited in the Code note is a held later event. Searches: current-law:usc (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09, 3 hits), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14, 0 hits) and later-events:ofr_catalog (3 hits, the three amendments above) were read with their coverage notes; no revocation was found in any of them.

The only ending is the execution of the supersession of Executive Order 11544 on issuance (Sec. 7, first half). No earlier revocation, supersession or own-terms end of any other section was found; the dossier flagged Sec. 2 with a report-deadline wording feature, but Sec. 2 contains no report, deadline or time limit (it concerns who may award the badge), so the feature identifies no end; the phrase 'for a period of at least one year' in Sec. 1 is an eligibility condition for each individual, not an end of the order.","independent_command_check":"Section 1 (establishment and eligibility), Section 2 (who awards), Section 3 (certificate and badge design), Section 4 (wearing during and after assignment), Section 5 (one badge per individual; posthumous award), Section 6 (wearing on the first day of duty) and Section 7 (supersession of Executive Order 11544 and grandfather proviso) are separate commands; only the supersession sentence of Section 7 was executed and ended, on issuance.","savings_check":"Section 7's proviso is the only savings language; it preserves wear permission for holders of badges awarded under Executive Order 11544. savings.reason: The proviso of Section 7 authorizes individuals previously awarded a Vice Presidential Service Badge under Executive Order 11544 to continue to wear it as part of their uniform. That permission is independent of the superseded order and has no end date in the held text; no held instrument ends it.
